title: How John Rush built an audience from zero: his 8-rule social playbook for founders
summary: John Rush shares the playbook he used to go from invisible to 50M views and 40k followers, which helped him reach 140,000 users with Unicorn Platform. He argues for one platform, followers as the KPI, deep expertise in one niche, and content aimed at your buyers rather than a broad audience.

principles.text: Focus 100% on one platform until you have several thousand followers and good content quality.
principles.quote: Until you reach several thousand followers and good content quality levels, creating content, engaging with people, and understanding the algorithm take hours daily.

principles.text: Pick Twitter as your training camp: shortest feedback loop, 10 practice posts a day. Writing skill transfers to every platform.
principles.quote: I suggest going with Twitter since it has the shortest feedback loop, and you can create 10 daily posts to practice.

principles.text: Track follower count, not views. Followers measure content quality because they follow authors they respect.
principles.quote: Don’t focus on pure views. Focus on followers.

principles.text: Stay on one topic until you break through. Scattershot topics produce unrepeatable virality.
principles.quote: The most typical mistake I see around is people trying to throw all sorts of topics, hoping to get lucky and viral with one. Even if this happens, you won’t be able to reproduce it later.

principles.text: Add your own experiments and experience to your topic; become a top 0.1% expert through thousands of hours.
principles.quote: You can’t just repost the known theory. You must add your own personal practice to it. This makes the information valuable.

principles.text: Not every follower counts. B2B founders need followers who buy; entertainment audiences don't convert.
principles.quote: I launched all my product via social media and got way more than 10 sales instantly, while having 20x fewer followers than him.
